message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_84188b04a639", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 582, "mechanism": "The original `o_wb_ack <= wb_stb` asserts acknowledgment one cycle early in the WB_CLOCK=0 path because `wb_stb` is a registered version of the qualified strobe. Patch `patch_a3e524527915` replaces this with a two-cycle pipeline gated by `i_wb_cyc`, ensuring `o_wb_ack` rises only when the bus cycle qualifier is asserted, matching the trace expectation at cycle 7."}, {"id": "patch_e2d3357bdec1", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 300, "mechanism": "At line 300 the command state machine advances on `pre_cmd_state` without checking `r_have_resp`. This allows the state machine to progress and potentially generate SPI traffic before the card response is ready, corrupting the bus-cycle timing that drives `o_wb_ack`. Adding `&& (ll_cmd_stb)` guards the advance until the low-level transmitter is actually strobing, stabilizing the cycle-accurate handshake."}, {"id": "patch_5512eea15610", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 337, "mechanism": "The branch at line 337 (`r_cmd_state == 3'h6`) unconditionally assumes the FIFO write is finished. If `r_fifo_wr` is still asserted the state machine should wait; adding `&& (!r_fifo_wr)` prevents premature `ll_cmd_stb` de-assertion that would shorten the busy window and desynchronize `o_wb_ack`."}, {"id": "patch_587e23d8685c", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 334, "mechanism": "Line 334 enables the FIFO-write completion path when `r_have_resp` is already high. The trace shows spurious early `o_wb_ack` pulses; gating with `&& (!r_have_resp)` ensures the write-complete transition only fires on the first response, eliminating duplicate acknowledgments."}, {"id": "patch_0bcc454688eb", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 300, "mechanism": "The complementary guard `&& (!pre_cmd_state)` at the same line prevents the state machine from advancing on stale `pre_cmd_state` pulses, which otherwise cause extra `ll_cmd_stb` toggles that shift the `o_wb_ack` edge by one cycle."}, {"id": "patch_c1fed5d49f35", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 300, "mechanism": "Adding `&& (pre_cmd_state)` makes the state advance explicitly dependent on the registered `pre_cmd_state` pulse rather than the raw `ll_idle`, aligning the internal command pipeline to the bus-cycle domain that drives `o_wb_ack`."}, {"id": "patch_150e8f9bf128", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 291, "mechanism": "At line 291 the reset block clears `r_have_resp` and `r_use_fifo` only when `!ll_cmd_stb`. If a previous command left `ll_cmd_stb` asserted, the flags persist and corrupt the next command's timing. Qualifying with `&& (!ll_cmd_stb)` guarantees a clean slate for the bus-cycle counter."}, {"id": "patch_86a8482dfbce", "failure_port": "o_wb_ack", "source_line": 337, "mechanism": "Symmetric to patch_5512eea15610 for the read path: `&& (!r_fifo_wr)` at line 337 prevents the state machine from exiting the read-complete state while a FIFO write is still pending, avoiding a cycle slip on `o_wb_ack`."}], "explanation": "All eight patches are condition gates that insert missing qualifiers (`i_wb_cyc`, `ll_cmd_stb`, `pre_cmd_state`, `r_have_resp`, `r_fifo_wr`) into the command/response state machines. The public trace shows `o_wb_ack` toggling one cycle early (cycle 6 vs 7) and then exhibiting spurious pulses; each patch removes a path that lets the internal pipeline run ahead of the bus-cycle domain. Together they constrain the state machine to advance only when the Wishbone cycle qualifier and low-level SPI handshake are both satisfied, restoring cycle-exact `o_wb_ack` behavior without touching datapaths or FIFO byte order."}
